title: Rebecca Kraft:
headline: A DSW sales associate explains the store's shoe take-back: donated shoes earn points, they go to Soles4Souls, and every pair comes back around. Nothing is wasted.
story: This is the donation explainer for the take-back at DSW. Your old shoes are not trash. A customer drops a pair in the bin and earns points, and the shoes go to Soles4Souls. On the day we filmed, Soles4Souls and the Boys and Girls Club gave every kid a new pair in the same store.

Rebecca Kraft, a part-time sales associate, tells it in her own words. Her last line is the point of the film: <q>it's a cycle and there's nothing being wasted</q>. The picture opens and closes on the DONATE HERE bin, so the cycle closes on screen too.
Loop: “What happens to my old shoes?” opens at 0:00 on the bin and closes at 0:33 on “it's a cycle”. Stakes: a pair in a closet helps no one; a pair in the bin goes to someone who needs it.
do: Open on the pair going into the DONATE HERE bin, with the hook text <q>Your old shoes = 50 points</q> already on screen at 0:00.
Use only Rebecca's answers. Lisa's questions are off camera: cut them and never caption them.
Start the third line cleanly on <q>The shoes that customers bring back</q>. No <q>So</q> before it.
Grade the B-roll to match her interview. Her graded clip is the look.
Keep the music audible under her voice from frame 1 to the end card.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00. The Soles4Souls name comes only on the end card.
Do not use the hand waving the shoes over the bin. Start when the pair goes in.
No soft or unclear B-roll. Every shot has one clear subject.
Do not use <q>so the shoes themselves or the materials of the shoes go to kids and adults who need them</q>. It is cut from this video.
Stop the points line at shoe account. Never write “Souls for Souls” on screen: it is Soles4Souls.
